notes.title: Refinements to Features from the Previous Patch 1.2.2
notes.notes:
This quick follow-up to our last update focuses on balancing previously introduced features, polishing audio and UI elements, refining enemy behavior, and fixing important bugs in portal zones and monster logic.


Polish

Mouse navigation in the Material Bank Altar menu is now smoother – no more twitching when hovering over material icons from below.

Added a sound effect for fireball projectile destruction.

Lowered the volume of Mourning Sister attacks.

Tweaked trap sounds (spike trap, rotating trap).

UI sounds now play correctly from both sides of stereo output.

More natural idle rotation for enemies in most scenes.

Reduced monster group size in one arena on Level 1 of the Temple of Discovery to prevent a difficulty spike.

Increased bonus material droppers in Level 1 of the Caves of Despair, where props are harder to find.

Made the charging effect for the first heavy attack in a combo more visible.


Bug Fixes

Secret dimensions behind portals are now safe to navigate and no longer cause instant death in certain levels.

Fixed an issue where monster packs could freeze mid-fight until one enemy was defeated.


More updates to come, under the watchful eyes of the ancient gods!

notes.title: Third Patch! v1.2.1
notes.notes:
This patch is a start of a journey towards better replayability of The book of Aaru with some major new features updates. 



New Features

All UI interactions now provide proper sound feedback. Actions like hover, select, or slider movement each have a dedicated sound.

Bonus hidden material spawners have been added to every dungeon to increase material collection potential.

Each dungeon now randomly selects 5 to 10 destroyable props and turns them into boosted material droppers with unique lighting and material type.

Boosted droppers yield 10 times the usual material amount.

Complete rework of how enemies spawn in combat arenas. Grouping and placement of enemies are now much more random, supporting the core principles of procedural generation used in roguelite dungeon design.



Polish

Polished the animation in the "monster in shadows" menu scene.

Fireball projectiles now trigger a visual effect when disappearing.

Dungeon infographic UI now shows which unique materials can be found in the given dungeon.

Black areas in outer environments have been covered with decoration.

Akhuu (healer enemy) now doesn't suffer from excesive idling between his actions

Some very big environment props removed from list of destroyable objects to prevent unnatural feeling of destruction

Animation of used healing fountain gives more clear feedback of being actually used

Level 1 of Temple of Discovery and Bastion have atmosphere closer to original intention (slightly warmer and darker) 



Fixes

Enemies such as Critter Hornet, Mourning Sister, or Rat Servant now correctly react to stun from parry, with no chance of invisible retaliation.

The Critter Hornet’s launch attack collider has been fixed in all cases where it was incorrectly dealing damage.

Some UI buttons have polished glow visual without pixelization

Rotating traps have better priority of sound emmiting


Thank you for playing and sharing your thoughts. Your feedback helps us move the game forward. As always, you’re welcome to comment under this post or reach out to us on Discord.

notes.title: Patch 1.2 - Enhanced Graphics Settings!
notes.notes:
We bring you an important update – a full graphical settings overhaul.
This update brings much deeper customization of graphical settings, adjusted to your possible hardware needs. In addition to expanding access to many graphics options, our secondary goal was to make the menu cleaner, more intuitive, and visually appealing.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/f7b4f3d94f3472f9158b0fb0760d42cc47b561cf.png"]
You can now toggle on or off many post-processing features, such as:
Bloom

Film grain

Depth of field

Motion blur

Chromatic aberration

While we recommend keeping these settings at their default values to experience the game’s intended visuals, we understand that some players may prefer to disable them due to performance or personal preference. The control is now in your hands.


We also added options for:
Shadow resolution and overall shadow quality

Anti-aliasing

Render scale


What we fixed or optimized:
A more reliable frame limiter for less powerful hardware

With this, we've also partially enabled control over V-Sync

Screen mode selection

Screen resolution options

Each setting now includes a clear description of what it does, our recommended value, and its expected impact on performance. All options and their descriptions have been fully localized into all 11 supported languages!



Alongside the graphical menu overhaul, we’ve also completed the implementation of the improved auto-aim feature mentioned in our previous update:

[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2092970/view/518589674441148505"][/dynamiclink]

Let us know if you’re missing any crucial settings or if the new options have helped improve your performance and overall experience. We'd love to hear your feedback!



This update also brings us one step closer to the official Steam Deck release, where optimization is crucial for smooth performance.

notes.title: Better Aim Helpers Update
notes.notes:
The Book of Aaru is a challenging roguelite, as it should be. But we also know that not everyone is looking for a try-hard experience. Some of you are here to enjoy the rich Egyptian Sci-fi world we've built, and want to let that sink in without the roguelite struggles.

To support a wider range of playstyles, we've always offered two aim-related helpers in combat: Aim-Assist and Lock-On Target. Now, with this update, we're making them more accessible, better explained, and easier to manage during gameplay.
[hr][/hr]How Do These Systems Work?
Aim-Assist is designed as a quality of life feature. It’s for players who want to stay in control of their aiming but wouldn’t mind a little help. With this option enabled, you still control rotation manually, but if your aim drifts slightly off target, within a small angle tolerance, the system gently nudges your attack back toward the enemy.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/ec4e5750b2f2d0337d99568bb3e858595a731c52.png"] 

Under the hood, this uses two invisible cones:

A tight cone that confirms you’re aiming closely enough to “attach” to an enemy.

A wider cone that helps reattach your aim if you momentarily slip off target after already locking on.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/6c60b91c793234e85a53a66e17125ed57e95d26c.png"]

Lock-On Target, on the other hand, is a more powerful assist, which completely lowers the difficulty of the game. It fully takes over your character’s rotation and always focuses on the nearest enemy, letting you concentrate purely on dodging and attacking. You can manually cycle through enemies as well, giving you full control over who to target next.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/03f004c5eb1448bd51d7d974db984d29754866e5.png"]
[hr][/hr]What’s New in This Update?
The most important change: clarity and accessibility.

Until now, many players weren’t aware these features even existed in the tutorial, it was easy to miss how to interact with these features. With this update:

The first time you plug in a controller, a pop-up explains both aim helpers and asks if you'd like to enable Lock-On by default or opt for a more challenging experience without it.

Once you make a choice, the game remembers your preferred default and automatically reapplies it whenever a level is loaded - even if you accidentally switched it mid-combat.

You can toggle either system on or off at any time during battle temporarily.

You can also change your default aim setting permanently via the controls options menu.

And for extra clarity, we’ve added new HUD icons that clearly show whether Aim-Assist or Lock-On Target is currently active all the time.
[hr][/hr]Got Feedback?
We’d love to hear what you think! If you have questions, suggestions, or want to share how the new system feels, drop a comment below or join the conversation on our Discord: https://discord.gg/UV72k3h7hy.


Thank you for playing, and good luck fighting off waves of demonic foes!

notes.title: Third Patch! v1.1.2 – Wall Escape Fixes & Better Parry
notes.notes:
This update focuses on tightening level design and improving the overall feel of combat. We've gone through all core scenes to reinforce boundaries, polish gameplay feedback, and make the early game experience a bit more forgiving, especially when it comes to parrying. 

Feature Improvements  [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/3ad53789ccd2a7f5a12ae7fa0d5c4823cfe2a246.png"]Scene Fixes & Wall Prevention
We have created a tool that lets us scan a scene and map out zones, based on weather they are covered by walls of sufficient height. Thanks to that, we were able to focus on preventing players from escaping the intended walkable areas and falling out of the world. Here’s what’s been addressed: 

All known spots where players could climb over walls and leave the map have been fixed.

Every main scene has been reviewed and updated with extra preventive measures to block unintended exits.

Note: Sandstorm-level scenes will receive the same treatment in an upcoming patch.

Destroyable objects placed on walls will now drop their materials next to the wall instead of on top, to prevent loot from getting stuck.

Certain cliffs, walls, and other big objects do not properly interact with projectiles

Minor object placement tweaks, added decorations, or overall small prop adjustments

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/d85c2887460cff227cd0cd88dab071f0e09cbf8a.png"]


Combat Polish - Parry Improvements
We’ve overhauled the parry system to better support learning and make early-game fights less punishing:

Parrying now always provides some form of damage protection, even on imperfect timing.

A successful parry now grants a short invulnerability window, in addition to deflecting the attack and stunning enemies.


New Visual Feedback - Heavy Attack Charging
We’ve added a new on-screen effect when charging up heavy attacks to help communicate timing and intention.



📢 We need your feedback!

Is the effect too distracting?

Is it barely visible on your screen or device?
Let us know - we want to fine-tune this visual until it feels just right.


Bug Fixes:
Minor localization corrections.

Thank you all for your continued support and feedback. As always, feel free to share your thoughts in the comments or over on our Discord: https://discord.gg/UV72k3h7hy!



See you in the Temple!

notes.title: Second Patch! v1.1.1
notes.notes:
Shortly after our first patch v1.1 released during launch week, we're back with another batch of improvements and fixes. This time, we focused primarily on improving the clarity of several in-game menus. We also made balance adjustments, especially to the time-bending ability. Last but not least, we addressed several situations where player progression could become blocked.


Bug Fixes
Fix for un-closeable Portal shortcut UI menu

Fixed an edge case situation where no action was possible if the inventory was full and the player chose an additional Glyph or Supportive Gear in the end-level reward menu

Fix for the immediate closing of inventory upon its opening

Player stats and inventory now carry over to the final arena of the All-Knowing Halls Dungeon as intended

The Green Dimension portal in the All-Knowing Halls Dungeon is fixed so that it does not softlock the player in the secret dimension

Popup numbers for any damage or heal indication cleaned from ghosting underlying black numbers in the bottom layer

Revealing Glyphs and Supportive Gear in the looting stage is no longer free

Dungeon UI data for times survived now updates with every win

The health bar of the Caves of Despair Dungeon Keeper is now visible immediately from the start of level 3 to showcase his health loss if the shortcut is not taken


Feature Improvements

Time Bending Overhaul
Popup numbers showcasing Time Essence gained are visually enhanced to an orange-purple style to match the rest of the Time Bending ability visuals

Streak indicator introduced into HUD UI around the Time Essence bar to showcase streak buildup and extinction

Streak capped at 7 build-ups to prevent broken builds where infinite Time Bending was possible

Streak is moderated down to limit the exponential growth of the bonus, but also to make it more satisfying from attack to attack


Blessing Screen Menu Overhaul
Animation for blessing added

An additional window with clearly calculated values of costs and to-be-blessed materials added

Warning hints for two different scenarios explaining why blessing is not possible

First: when the player does not have enough materials and needs to collect more

Second: when the player needs to bless a larger portion at once to overcome the price of blessing

Localization into 11 languages for all new texts

Prevention against blessing if the resulting amount would be 0

Resetting the menu on exit from any stage to make re-entry into the menu clean every time

Visual update of buttons and fonts for clarity and aesthetic polish

Matched visual update is also in the Material screen under the player inventory menu

Highlighting materials that are being interacted with during bthe lessing

Prevention against mouse hovering breaking the navigation with keyboard across the menu

Increased amount of kept materials on death from 15% to 20%


Polish
Added Attribute Altar to the end of level 3 in the First Laboratory Dungeon so the player can use newly collected shards on the trial path

Minor various scene updates for better functioning traps, and better positioned obstacles and decorations



To see the full list of updates since release, you can also check out the previous update log:



[dynamiclink href="https://steamcommunity.com/games/2092970/announcements/detail/518589049004361709"][/dynamiclink]

Enjoy the adventure!

notes.title: Glyph Perk System: A Deep Dive & Graphical Update
notes.notes:
Get ready to dive deeper into the world of Glyphs! We've revamped our perk system with fresh visuals and enhanced descriptions. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/a7003f5d39e587fa4f8288912e7c0194d3c19010.png
What’s new?

 Each Glyph now has its own unique icon that matches its specific ability.
 Hand-designed icons are made to be easily recognizable.
 Icons more closely represent the category and purpose of each upgrade.

How our perk system works? 


Application categorizes Glyphs into five types:


 Are you an offensive powerhouse? Unleash devastating attacks with Offensive Glyphs.
 Prefer a defensive stance? Defensive Glyphs provide protective bonuses, such as reducing damage received from dangerous traps scattered throughout the depths of Aaru.
 Want a versatile arsenal? Utility Glyphs offer a wide array of abilities, from combat rewards after successful parries to lightning attacks jumping between enemies activated by well performed combos.
 Looking to strike it rich? Increase your chances of finding valuable treasures or larger quantities of them or gain a chance to receive bonus rewards for your spent currency with Riches Glyphs!
 Ready to bend time to your will? Time Altering Glyphs enhance your ability to Bend Time, for example enabling you to unleash a powerful shockwave when this unique ability is activated.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/95f5d0bcac1a6f1385e2d27c2cfb667e887ddc07.png
Risk divides Glyphs into three tiers,
but remember, every choice comes with a downfall. Stat-based Glyphs offer subtle enhancements, while Gameplay Altering Glyphs unlock new abilities or evolve existing ones. Dare to take higher risk? Two-edged Glyphs provide powerful benefits but also come with drawbacks.


 Stat-based: These Glyphs provide passive, low-risk enhancements, subtly boosting your abilities in the background - like increasing your chance to deal critical damage or heighten your stamina recovery.
 Gameplay altering: These Glyphs unlock new abilities or evolve existing ones. As a result, they carry a moderate risk as your skill level will determine how effectively you can harness these enhancements.
 Two-edged: These Glyphs offer high-risk, high-reward perks. They significantly boost your character in one aspect but also make you weaker in another. For example, with a curse of Seth your attacks will gain immense power, but you'll need to engage in constant combat or you start losing your health.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42788407/96a7548267cecef2bec5daabda265bd0f5a60e1b.png
Choose wisely and tailor your Glyph loadout to fit your playstyle!
